commits.message:
feat(microsoft-graph): support watching a specific mail folder, not just Inbox

Root cause of the "received in Outlook but never processed" report:
a mailbox-side rule was silently filing real job postings from
jobs.nvoids.com into a "Nvoids" subfolder of jobs@jobfynder.com.
Hermes' Graph subscription only ever watched Inbox -- notifications
only fire for the exact folder a subscription names, so those 17
postings (confirmed via the Graph API directly) were completely
invisible to Hermes the whole time, with nothing about the Inbox
subscription itself unhealthy or slow. The pipeline was never "slow"
for this mail; it never saw it at all.

HERMES_MS_GRAPH_MAILBOXES entries now accept an optional
":FolderDisplayName" suffix (configured_mailbox_targets(), replacing
the plain address list configured_mailboxes() used to return
directly -- that function stays for callers that only want distinct
addresses, e.g. the status endpoint). A custom folder can't be
addressed by name the way "Inbox" can in the Graph resource path, so
_resolve_folder_resource() looks its id up from the mailbox's folder
listing by displayName before creating the subscription.

Storage/result keys stay exactly the bare mailbox address for the
default (no folder suffix) case -- zero format change for the
existing jobs@/hotlists@ Inbox subscriptions, confirmed by every
existing hermes-850-live-fetch-check.py assertion passing unchanged.
A named-folder target gets its own "mailbox:FolderName" key instead,
so the same mailbox can hold both an Inbox subscription and a
subfolder one side by side without one overwriting the other in
subscriptions.json.

.env.example's HERMES_MS_GRAPH_MAILBOXES now includes
jobs@jobfynder.com:Nvoids alongside the two existing entries, with
the new syntax documented above it.

New coverage: test_graph_sync_creates_subscription_for_named_folder
in hermes-850-live-fetch-check.py, covering the full path including
the folder-name-to-id lookup. Full regression suite (16 checks) green
against a freshly reset schema.
